(2) 2025-07-03 EQUITY INDEX. STATUS VOCABULARY, as used below. 'closed' - the family publishes no tradeable session on the date. 'early_close' - a session runs and ends earlier than the family's normal grid for that weekday, and close_instant carries the stated instant. 'modified' - the published event list differs from the normal grid in some way other than an earlier final close (a missing evening leg, a missing final close, a pre-open at a different time, a trade date that rolls past the holiday). 'normal' - the published event list and its trade dates equal the family's normal grid for that weekday. 'unknown' - only a publication known to be superseded survives for the date, and it is not carried.

SOURCE. cmegroup.com refuses this machine directly (HTTP 403, 'This IP address is blocked due to suspected web scraping activity'), so live pages and service calls were read through the public reader https://r.jina.ai/<url> and history through the Wayback Machine with id_ replay. CME no longer publishes a per-holiday hours PDF or XLS: from the 2025 calendar year the holiday hours ARE the interactive table on https://www.cmegroup.com/trading-hours.html ('Please note that with the 2025 calendar year the CME Group will be providing downloadable holiday calendars for Globex and incorporating with Regular Trading hours into one location'), and every 'Holiday Schedule' link on the Holiday Calendar page points at that page. The per-holiday PDFs that do exist for 2025/2026 ('...-holiday-settlement-times-<year>.pdf', '<year>-...-clearing-advisory.pdf', 'otc-...pdf') carry settlement-price and clearing-cycle information only and state no trading hours; the MLK-2025 clearing advisory routes trading hours back to 'CME Group Holiday Calendar / CME Group Trading Hours'. Those two were retrieved and indexed to document that the channel was read and is not a session source (LAW-SESSION-NOT-EXPIRY).

CHANNEL AND TIER. The rows below come from https://www.cmegroup.com/services/trading-hours-by-product?...&fromEventDate=&toEventDate= - the endpoint the trading-hours page itself calls to render its per-asset-class Holiday Hours table. That is the operator's own trading-hours service, so T2 under LAW-PRIMARY-SOURCES, not T1. It was validated against the T1 rendering: for Thanksgiving 2026 the page prints rows labelled Interest Rates / Equities / Energy / Grains / FX / Metals / Livestock / Dairy / Cryptocurrencies / Lumber and each printed row matches the service rows for ZN / ES / CL / ZC / 6E / GC / LE / CSC / BTC / LBR event for event (e.g. printed 'Friday 27 Nov 2026 | Interest Rates | TRADE DATE: Fri 27 Nov 12:15 closed' = service ZN eventDate 2026-11-27 12:15 closed, trade date 2026-11-27). The saved rendering is live/trading-hours-live.md.

ZONE. Verbatim from the page: 'Trading hours are subject to change and are in U.S. Central Time unless otherwise stated.' Every instant recorded below is therefore CT as printed; CME prints no ET column in this channel, so no ET value is asserted. The page's free-text Holiday Notes do print CT/ET pairs, but only for TAS/TAM trade-type variants (e.g. 'Gold TAS: Early close 11:30 CT / 12:30 ET'), which are not the family sessions.

EVENT VOCABULARY, verbatim from the same page: PREOPEN 'Order Entry, modification, and cancel are allowed. No order matching.'; OPEN 'Start of continuous trading phase. Order matching begins.'; Paused 'Interruption of continuous trading. Only order cancellation is allowed. No order matching.'; pcp (POST CLOSE - PREOPEN) 'Allows GTC/GTD orders only placement, modification, and cancellation. No order matching.'; closed 'Final Close of the date. Day and GTD (current trade date) orders are eliminated.' This distinction matters: on the Monday holidays CME does NOT publish a 'closed' event at noon - it publishes a preopen, i.e. matching stops but the trade date does not end and the whole Sunday-evening-through-Monday span carries the following business day's trade date. Those rows are marked early_close with the instant, and the note says the event type is preopen.

ENUMERATION. Archive CDX was run first over cmegroup.com/tools-information/holiday-calendar*, cmegroup.com/trading-hours* and cmegroup.com/services/trading-hours* (results saved under cdx/). CME's forward holiday LIST (services/trading-hours-filters) starts at Labor Day 2026-09-07 and runs to New Year 2028-01-01, but the trading-hours-by-product service itself is NOT limited to that list: it still answers for past windows back to Thanksgiving 2025 (verified 2026-09-12 - every window from 2025-11-26 forward returns a schedule, while the eight windows New Year 2025 through Labor Day 2025 return the products with empty schedules, so its retention edge falls between Labor Day 2025 and Thanksgiving 2025). The 2025 and 2026-Jan..Jul rows were originally taken from Wayback captures of the same endpoint, 2026-09 onward from live retrieval, and the repair round of 2026-09-12 read the nine still-served past windows live (D54-D67). Where more than one capture of a window exists the most recent was used; the fresh CDX run of 2026-09-12 re-checked this window by window and the one window where it did not hold - Thanksgiving 2025 - was re-sourced (see D09/D09P below). CME's own forward holiday list (services/trading-hours-filters, saved as api/filters.json) supplied the holiday dates and each holiday's start/end period for 2026-09-07 through 2028-01-01.

BASELINE. 'Status' is stated against CME's own non-holiday grid, taken from a clean reference week 2026-10-18..2026-10-24 pulled from the same service (live/normal/*.json), not from any pattern assumed by me. Each family row's verbatim carries the published event list AND that normal grid so the comparison is re-checkable. The per-date, per-product rows with baselines and deviation flags are in raw/cme-2025-2027/FINAL_ROWS.json; a readable review is FINAL_REVIEW.txt.

GROUPS. The ten groups CME prints map to these products, which are exactly the ten the trading-hours page itself queries: Equity Index=ES (E-mini S&P 500), Interest Rates=ZN (10-Year T-Note), FX=6E (Euro FX), Energy=CL (Crude Oil), Metals=GC (Gold), Grains & Oilseeds=ZC (Corn), Livestock=LE (Live Cattle), Cryptocurrency=BTC (Bitcoin), Dairy=CSC (Cash-Settled Cheese), Lumber=LBR (Lumber). From Thanksgiving 2025 forward the Nikkei-specific line (NKD Nikkei/USD, NIY Nikkei/JPY), soybeans (ZS), wheat (ZW), lean hogs (HE) and Class III milk (DC) were pulled as a second id set (id=168,167,320,323,19,27); where they appear they track ES (Nikkei), ZC (ZS/ZW), LE (HE) and CSC (DC) event for event, with one exception worth naming: on Good Friday 2026 NKD/NIY close 08:15 CT with ES, not 10:15 CT with ZN/6E/BTC.

STRUCTURE OF THE ROWS. One holidays[] entry per CME holiday. Inside it, families[] carries one row per (product group set, date): the holiday's own date is given for every group including the ones that ran normally, and the adjacent dates in CME's own window (eve, day after, the Sunday evening leg, and the Saturday sessions) are given only where CME publishes something other than the normal grid. Groups that share an identical published event list on a date are listed together in one row. 'family' ends with '| date YYYY-MM-DD' naming the date the row governs. Note codes N1..N18 and EC are expanded in raw/cme-2025-2027/INDEX.md (N17 and N18 are defined in raw/cme-2025-2027-fix/INDEX.md and appended to the original INDEX.md): N17 = no day session on the holiday; only a 16:00 CT pre-open and a 17:00 CT open, both already carrying the next business day's trade date. N18 = the published event TIMES equal the family's normal grid for that weekday, but the re-open carries a trade date that skips the following closed holiday, so the date does carry a holiday trade-date roll. N19 = 24/7 Cryptocurrency grid on a FRIDAY holiday: the 16:00 CT final-close event is published but carries the following Monday's trade date, so the holiday's own trade date has no session and no settlement and the whole day rolls (distinct from N10, where on a Monday or Thursday holiday the 16:00 CT event is omitted altogether, and from N8, because on a normal Friday the 16:00 CT close carries that Friday's own trade date).

WHAT THE DATA SHOWS, in outline. Monday/Thursday-Friday holidays (MLK, Presidents', Memorial, Labor, Juneteenth 2025, Thanksgiving) halt Equity Index and Interest Rates at 12:00 CT and Energy and Metals at 13:30 CT with a 17:00 CT reopen; FX and (pre-24/7) Cryptocurrency keep the ordinary 16:00-17:00 CT pause; Grains & Oilseeds have no day session and open 19:00 CT for the next trade date; Livestock, Lumber and (on some) Dairy do not trade at all. Good Friday 2025 and 2027 are a full Globex closure for every family (crypto excepted in 2027, which is 24/7 from 2026-05-29 and trades through). Good Friday 2026 is the exception CME itself flags, verbatim from the T1 operator page D50 (line 2498 of html/trading-hours-20250830.html): 'Due to the US Employment Situation Release on April 3, 2026, CME Group Equities, FX, Cryptocurrency and Interest Rate products will have unique Closes and Settlements for trade date April 3rd.' The same list continues, still D50: 'All other CME, CBT, NYMEX and COMEX products will have their settlements copied from April 2nd to April 3rd.' and 'No trading for Friday April 3th  trade date in observence of Good Friday.' (sic). D50 is T1 corroboration that Equities, FX, Cryptocurrency and Interest Rates traded that day and everything else did not, but it states no instants; the instants - Equities close 08:15 CT, Interest Rates, FX and Cryptocurrency 10:15 CT - come only from the T2 service document D14, which is what those rows cite. Independence Day (2025-07-04, 2026-07-03, 2027-07-05) and Juneteenth 2026/2027 run a 12:00 CT final close for the 24-hour groups with Grains, Livestock, Lumber and Dairy shut. The day after Thanksgiving is an early close at 12:15 CT (Equity Index, Interest Rates, Nikkei), 13:45 CT (FX, Energy, Metals, pre-24/7 Crypto) and 12:05 CT (Grains, Livestock, Lumber), with Dairy shut. Christmas Eve is 12:15 CT (Equity Index, Interest Rates, Nikkei), 12:45 CT (FX, Energy, Metals), 12:05 CT (Grains, Livestock, Lumber) and 12:00 CT (Dairy); Christmas Day and New Year's Day are full closures. New Year's Eve and the Thursday before Good Friday are a normal 16:00 CT final close with no evening reopen.

TWO THINGS WORTH FLAGGING TO THE CRATE. (1) After the Friday holidays of 2026 and 2027 CME publishes a SATURDAY session for the 24-hour groups - 2026-06-20, 2026-07-04 and 2027-06-19 all carry 'open 05:00 CT / closed 17:00 CT' with the following Monday's trade date, against a normally empty Saturday. These are in the rows as status modified, note N11. Saturday 2026-04-04 after Good Friday 2026 does NOT carry one (checked against the service for window 2026-04-02..04). (2) From 2026-05-29 Cryptocurrency is 24/7, and how a holiday shows up depends on the weekday. On a MONDAY or THURSDAY holiday the 16:00 CT daily final close is omitted outright and only '16:01 preopen / 16:02 open' is published (note N10). On a FRIDAY holiday the 16:00 CT close IS printed, but it carries the FOLLOWING MONDAY's trade date rather than the holiday's own, so the holiday still has no settlement and no trade date of its own and the whole day rolls (note N19 - the six rows 2026-06-19, 2026-07-03, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01, 2027-03-26 and 2027-06-18). Either way trading itself is continuous; what the holiday removes is the trade date, which is why those rows carry status 'closed' under DESIGN decisions D1 and D9. The Saturday case is different again and genuinely normal: 2028-01-01 prints '02:00 closed; 03:45 preopen; 04:00 open (trade date 2028-01-03)', which is the ordinary Saturday grid.

NOT CME GLOBEX HOLIDAYS. Columbus Day and Veterans Day appear nowhere in CME's Globex holiday list (api/filters.json) even though CME publishes clearing advisories, settlement-times PDFs and OTC notices for them; Globex trades a normal session on both. They are therefore not recorded as holidays here.

RESIDUAL RISK. Trading hours are usually finalized approximately two weeks prior to the holiday.' A fresh CDX enumeration of cmegroup.com/services/trading-hours-by-product* (raw/cme-2025-2027-fix/cdx/cdx_thbp_all_fix.json, 688 rows, retrieved 2026-09-12) confirms each of those eight windows has no capture later than 2024-12-20 (the New Year window has a second, earlier capture at 2024-07-08T16:14:39Z), so those rows are CME's published future as of 2024-12-20 rather than a post-finalisation statement. They are internally consistent with the 2026 and 2027 rows for the same holidays, which are sourced from later captures and from live retrieval. The three remaining 2025/26 windows DO have post-holiday captures and are sourced from them: Thanksgiving 2025 (45 captures, latest 2026-01-29T01:23:09Z = D09), Christmas 2025 (45 captures, latest 2026-01-29T01:23:09Z, content-identical to the 2026-01-29T01:21:59Z bytes already saved as D10 - re-fetched and compared in this round) and New Year 2026 (51 captures, latest 2026-07-22T11:42:22Z, content-identical schedule for schedule to D11's 2026-06-19T11:41:05Z bytes - re-fetched and compared in this round).
